newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures up, May capped at $1,650.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures up, May capped at $1,650.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures ended Friday higher but failed to make further headway on the upside in the afternoon despite advancing New York-listed arabica futures.
Traders said spot May was capped through the day at $1,650 a tonne on origin hedge selling, notably from Indonesia.
May last hit the $1,650 mark on April 1. The Indonesians, faced with growing supplies from its new crop harvest, had been noticably absent in the last few days awaiting lucrative prices.
Although the new robusta crop could be 10-20 percent down from the last season's 7.5 to 8.0 million bags, the yield was still relatively large compared with the more recent seasons.
"At one stage, New York was five to six cents higher and London wasn't reacting," said one trader. "The origins were obviously keeping the market down."
But the market still finished up on balance on earlier speculative and trade buying. May and London's benchmark July were each up $20 at $1,640 and $1,663 respectively.

Overall volume was 5,007 lots which included May/July switches and against actuals. May/July was seen traded at $20-$25 under, weaker compared against the past weeks when the switches traded at level money.
New York forged ahead on Friday, fuelled by speculative buying amid mounting supply woes. July was driven to a high of 194.25 cents a lb but failed to clear the key 196 cents resistance.
By 1635 GMT, the contract was traded at 192.75.
Immediately, the market is bracing for possible Colombian
truck drivers strike due to take place on Sunday.
